data.name: Kasra
data.gender_notes: Kasra is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Persian word 'kasra', which originally meant 'chest' or 'fortress'. The name symbolizes strength, courage, and protection. The name Kasra carries the meaning “Chest, fortress, strong” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Persian, Arabic, Urdu. Parents who choose Kasra usually hope their child will grow to embody chest, fortress, strong and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the fortress of the heart, which protects and houses the soul.
data.etymology: Kasra belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Chest, fortress, strong.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kasra total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: كسرة
in_arabic.meaning: كسرة تعني انكسار أو هزيمة في اللغة العربية
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم كسرة هو مشتق من الفعل كسر، وهو يعني الانكسار أو الهزيمة. في اللغة العربية، يُستخدم هذا الاسم للإشارة إلى الشخص الذي يتحمل الكثير من التحديات والصعوبات في حياته، ويتميز بالصبر والتحمل. وقد ورد ذكر هذا الاسم في بعض الأحاديث النبوية الشريفة، حيث كان يُطلق على بعض الصحابة رضي الله عنهم.

in_urdu.name: کسری
in_urdu.meaning: کسری کا مطلب ٹوٹنا یا شکست کھانا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: کسری نام عربی زبان کے الفاظ سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے ٹوٹنا یا شکست کھانا۔ یہ نام ان شخصیتوں کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو زندگی میں بہت ساری چیلنجز اور مشکلات کا سامنا کرتے ہیں، لیکن وہ صبر اور استقامت کے ساتھ ان کا सामना کرتے ہیں۔ جنوبی ایشیاء میں مسلم کمیونٹی میں اس نام کا خاص اہمیت ہے، جہاں یہ نام بہادری اور استقامت کی علامت کے طور پر دیکھا جاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: कसरा
in_hindi.meaning: कसरा का अर्थ है टूटना या हारना
in_hindi.long_meaning: कसरा नाम अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है टूटना या हारना। यह नाम उन व्यक्तियों के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जो जीवन में कई चुनौतियों और कठिनाइयों का सामना करते हैं, लेकिन वे धैर्य और सहनशीलता के साथ उनका सामना करते हैं। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में इस नाम का विशेष महत्व है, जहां यह नाम बहादुरी और दृढ़ता का प्रतीक माना जाता है।

in_pashto.name: کسری
in_pashto.meaning: کسری د ټوټې یا ماتې معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: د کسری نوم په عربي ژبه کې د کسر فعل څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې معنی یې ټوټې یا ماتې ده. دا نوم د هغو کسانو لپاره کارول کیږي چې په ژوند کې ډیری ننګونې او مشکلات سره مخ کیږي، مګر دوی د صبر او استقامت سره مقابله کوي. په افغان او پښتون دود کې، دا نوم د زړورتیا او مقاومت نښه په توګه لیدل کیږي.

in_english.name: Kasra
in_english.meaning: Kasra means breaking or defeat, derived from Arabic roots
in_english.long_meaning: The name Kasra originates from the Arabic verb 'kasara,' which translates to 'to break' or 'defeat.' Etymologically, it is linked to the Arabic root 'k-s-r,' which appears in various Quranic verses and Hadiths, symbolizing resilience and strength in the face of challenges. Historically, the name has been used in Islamic tradition to signify a person who embodies courage and perseverance. In modern times, Kasra is used across different Muslim cultures, reflecting its enduring significance and appeal as a name that conveys powerful virtues.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Battuta's Travels: Ibn Battuta describes visiting the ancient city of Kasra in Iran, which was a significant caravan station on the Silk Road. The city was also known as the 'Grave of Hosein', referring to the martyrdom of Imam Hosein at the Battle of Karbala in 65 AH (680 AD).
historical_references.context: Caravan station on the Silk Road, Grave of Imam Hosein

historical_references.reference: The History of al-Tabari (Vol. III): Al-Tabari recounts the story of the Battle of Jalula in 115 AH (733 AD) between the Arab Caliphate and the Marwans. The battle took place near the city of Kasra, which was then the capital city of the Marwanids. The Arab forces were able to secure a significant victory, which marked the end of the Second Fitna (civil war) in the Islamic Caliphate.
historical_references.context: Capital city of the Marwanids, Battle site of the Second Fitna
